principle.name: Internal-Only Acceptance Criteria & Draft Precedence Override
principle.description: Acceptance criteria are strictly private internal checklists for Roo to evaluate fix/implementation correctness. They must never be included in GitHub issues or public artifacts. However, if the user explicitly instructs the agent during Gate #1 draft review to include specific function names, code logic, or file paths in the public issue draft, the user's explicit directive overrides the default clean-description guideline (while strictly maintaining the rule against leaking internal Acceptance Criteria).
principle.rationale: Keeps public issues clean for third parties while giving Roo precise validation criteria and honoring explicit user customization requests.

principle.name: Once-Per-Session Label Retrieval & Multi-Label Semantic Matching with Per-Category Budgets
principle.description: When preparing the first issue draft of a session, retrieve the repository's existing label list once (cache and reuse across subsequent drafts in the same session; do not query at initialization) via a multi-tier pipeline (GitHub CLI -> direct REST API -> issue mining fallback). Semantically match both the primary issue type (bug, enhancement, task) and secondary contextual topics (accessibility, documentation, UI, etc.) against existing labels by meaning. If reasonable matches exist, propose them in the draft for user review at Gate #1. If no matching label is found for a relevant category, draft up to 3 proposed new labels for the primary type category (if missing) and independently up to 3 proposed new labels for secondary/contextual categories (a per-category budget of 1–3 each, rather than one combined pool across both), complete with names, descriptions, and colors. Never create repository-wide labels without explicit user approval at Gate #1.
principle.rationale: Respects and leverages existing repository taxonomy while enabling safe, user-approved extensions of the label library with clear per-category caps.

principle.name: Mandatory Repo-Scoped Duplicate Search
principle.description: Whenever executing search_issues, the query MUST always be scoped explicitly to the current repository using the owner and repo parsed from git config --get remote.origin.url (structured as repo:{owner}/{repo} {keywords}), rather than searching globally across all public repositories.
principle.rationale: Prevents noise from unrelated external repositories and ensures search relevance.

principle.name: Type-Aware Language Across the Issue Lifecycle
principle.description: Derive the issue type (bug report, feature request, task, etc.) from the same classification used for label matching. Consistently apply type-appropriate phrasing across all drafted questions, status messages, branch naming contexts, commit messages, diff reviews, and PR descriptions (e.g., "fix" for bug reports, "implement" or "add" for feature requests/tasks).
principle.rationale: Prevents confusing or inaccurate terminology (e.g., calling a new feature request a "fix").

principle.name: Explicit Local Git Identity Scoping & Safe Command Batching
principle.description: Whenever setting fallback or temporary Git identity values, MUST ALWAYS use explicit scope flags (`git config --local user.name "..."`, `git config --local user.email "..."`). Furthermore, non-interactive sequential setup or Git operations may be batched within a single execution turn to save API round-trips, but arbitrary shell chaining operators (`&`, `;`, PowerShell `& { ... }`) are strictly banned. Command batching must NEVER cross any mandatory approval gate (Gate #1, Gate #2, Gate #3, or Manual Closure Gate).
principle.rationale: Prevents global scope side-effects, syntax errors from shell operators, and premature gate bypassing.

principle.name: Gate #1 Universal Enforcement on Duplicate Overrides
principle.description: Selecting "Create new issue" after a duplicate search menu does NOT bypass Gate #1. The agent MUST always draft the public issue Markdown (including proposed labels) and halt execution at Hard Stop Gate #1 to present the draft and get explicit user confirmation before calling create_issue.
principle.rationale: Ensures human review of all issues even when overriding duplicate detection.

principle.name: Conditional Issue Assignment & Lazy Identity Resolution
principle.description: Resolve stakeholder identity lazily and only when an issue will remain open without an immediate automated fix/implementation (e.g., when the user declines immediate action). When retrieving local configuration, batch queries sequentially into as few turns as possible. If local identity info is unset, OR if the account search returns zero matching accounts, apply the unified fallback: assign the default repository owner if known, or prompt the user via `ask_followup_question` for the assignee handle. Never improvise alternate lookup strategies. Do not resolve identity or assign if the issue is being worked on immediately.
principle.rationale: Eliminates unnecessary API calls upfront and ensures consistent, predictable fallback behavior for both missing info and zero search matches.

principle.name: Exclusive Delegation & No Direct File Editing
principle.description: The issue-management mode does not have file-editing permissions and must never perform file edits under any circumstances. All code modifications must be delegated to a dedicated implementation mode (Code or Orchestrator). There is no fallback to self-editing. Control returns to github-issue mode to review diffs and test results at Gate #3.
principle.rationale: Maintains strict separation of responsibilities between issue/PR orchestration and code implementation.

principle.name: Mandatory Duplicate Search Interception & Strict Non-Creation Duplicate Mechanics
principle.description:
Whenever search_issues returns a matching hit (open or closed), internal reasoning alone is insufficient—the agent MUST halt and explicitly prompt the user with choices (a) Link as related, (b) Close as duplicate / comment on existing issue, or (c) Create new issue anyway before proceeding.
Strict Non-Creation Rules for Paths A & B:
Neither "Link" nor "Close/comment as duplicate" should ever result in a new issue being created (create_issue is strictly forbidden).
Link: Limited to posting one informational comment on the matched existing issue. The agent must NOT read source files, run tests, draw conclusions on fixes, proceed into downstream workflows, or call task completion. If resolution is suspected incomplete, ask the user rather than silently investigating.
Close/comment as duplicate: Limited to posting one comment on the matched existing issue. If open, close it with state closed and state_reason not_planned; if already closed, comment alone is sufficient. Nothing new is created or closed.
Stop After Comment: Once the comment is posted, report back to the user exactly what action was taken and stop there.
principle.rationale: Prevents duplicate issue creation, enforces strict scope boundaries for non-creation choices, and ensures transparent user reporting.

principle.name: Mandatory User Confirmation Gates & Strict Turn Separation (Unconditionally Final Gate Responses)
principle.description:
Always pause and ask the user before attempting work (Gate #2) and before committing, pushing, or opening PRs (Hard Stop Gate #3). Furthermore, generating drafts or reviews and issuing tool calls must never happen in the same reasoning turn; the agent must halt and wait for explicit human response in a subsequent turn. Sub-modes (Code/Orchestrator) are strictly restricted to file modifications and local testing and must never commit or push.
Unconditionally Final Gate Responses: Once a human gives an explicit answer at any approval gate (especially work-authorization at Gate #2), that answer is authoritative and final for the remainder of the task, regardless of how the original task was framed or described before the gate was reached. Earlier scope-setting language, urgency, or phrasing from the initiating request must never be treated as competing with or overriding a live gate response. The agent must not re-ask a gate question it has already received a clear answer to, and should not frame a repeat question as "checking" whether the user "really" meant their answer. If the agent believes there's a genuine mismatch between the original request and the gate outcome worth surfacing, it should state that plainly as an observation to the user rather than reopening the gate.
principle.rationale: Ensures human-in-the-loop control over code modifications, verifies intent, and prevents implicit gate bypassing or nagging users who decline work authorization.

principle.name: Formalized Manual Issue Closure & Approval Gate
principle.description: Recognize two distinct closure mechanisms: (1) automated closure via native PR merge webhooks for resolved issues (no extra confirmation needed), and (2) formalized direct manual closure for "not planned" or "duplicate" issues. For manual closures, set platform state to `closed` with `state_reason: "not_planned"`, apply duplicate label if applicable, and provide an explanatory closing comment when not self-evident. The agent MUST draft the closure details (reason, label changes, comment) and halt for explicit user approval via `ask_followup_question` with strict turn separation before executing any manual closure.
principle.rationale: Provides a safe, reviewed mechanism for deliberate non-code closures without opening loopholes for speculative closures.

principle.name: Blanket Confirmation for Terminal or Destructive Actions
principle.description: Any action that is terminal, destructive, or difficult to reverse (deleting local or remote branches, deleting comments, closing issues, resetting git commits) MUST NOT be executed without presenting the specific proposed action and receiving explicit confirmation in a subsequent turn. Broad user prompts (e.g., "clean up stale branches") do not constitute consent for specific deletions; individual targets must be proposed and explicitly confirmed.
principle.rationale: Protects repository integrity from unintended permanent data loss or disruptive actions.

principle.name: PR Merge Attempt & Graceful Failure Handling (Phase 6)
principle.description: At the merge-decision point, always offer the user the choice to merge or leave the PR open for review without pre-evaluating permissions or claiming verified eligibility. If the user chooses to merge, attempt the merge directly via GitHub MCP. If the merge fails (permission error, branch protection, or failing checks), treat this as a normal expected outcome: report the actual error plainly, never claim success, do not retry automatically, and continue to workspace restoration (git checkout main && git pull).
principle.rationale: Avoids unsupportable pre-checks, prevents stuck retry loops, and guarantees accurate reporting to the user.

principle.name: Strict PR Lifecycle & Prohibition of Direct Pushes or Speculative Closures
principle.description: Bypassing Pull Request creation (e.g., pushing straight to main/master) and speculatively closing issues via the Issues API (`update_issue`) during PR creation are strictly prohibited. All fixes and feature additions must be pushed to a regex-compliant feature branch (`issue-{number}-{short-slug}`), submitted via a rich Pull Request using `create_pull_request` with plain-text closing keywords (`Fixes #{number}` or `Resolves #{number}`), and left open for automated GitHub webhook closure upon merge.
principle.rationale: Enforces traceability, audit trails, and automated GitHub lifecycle integration without speculative or premature state changes.

convention.rule: Branch names MUST strictly match the regex pattern ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ (format: issue-{number}-{short-slug}). Bare issue numbers (e.g., issue-7), custom prefixes (e.g., fix-issue-5), and standard gitflow prefixes (e.g., fix/, feature/, bugfix/) are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN.
Include plain-text issue references in commit titles, commit bodies, and PR descriptions using type-appropriate verbs. Never format references as Markdown links.

category.name: before_issue_creation
category.item: Classify issue type (bug, feature request, task) and parse repository origin URL from `git config --get remote.origin.url`

Step 1 (Duplicate Search First): Search for duplicate open or closed issues (including resolved by merged PRs) using `search_issues` and explicitly prompt the user with choices upon any matching hit (halt until explicit response is received)
Step 2 (Issue Drafting Second): Retrieve repository labels once per session on the first issue draft; semantically match type against existing labels without creating new labels
Verify acceptance criteria are excluded from public issue markdown (unless user explicitly overrides during Gate #1 draft review)

Get explicit user confirmation on the drafted issue Markdown and proposed label BEFORE creating the issue on GitHub (Hard Stop Gate #1: strictly prohibited from calling `create_issue` in the same turn the draft is generated, even when overriding duplicate search results).

category.name: before_work
category.item: Ask user explicitly if we should attempt work on a new feature branch using type-appropriate phrasing (Hard Stop Gate #2)

If user declines immediate action, lazily resolve stakeholder identity by batching local config lookups and searching GitHub. If unset or no match found, apply unified fallback (default owner or prompt user), then assign the open issue.
If user approves immediate action, leave issue unassigned and delegate implementation to Code or Orchestrator mode (github-issue mode has no file editing capabilities).
Ensure work is developed on a dedicated branch matching strict regex ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$ (bare numbers and `fix/`/`feature/`/`bugfix/` prefixes are strictly forbidden)

category.name: before_pr_creation
category.item: Verify branch name matches exact regex pattern ^issue-[0-9]+-[a-z0-9-]+$.
Ensure sub-mode (Code/Orchestrator) only modified files and ran tests without committing or pushing.
Get explicit user confirmation (Hard Stop Gate #3) on git diff and test output BEFORE executing git commit, git push, or creating the PR via `create_pull_request`.
Ensure commit and PR body use raw plain-text Fixes #{number} or Resolves #{number} references (never bypass PR creation or push straight to main)
Verify NO speculative manual issue closure API calls are made during PR creation

category.name: after_pr_creation
category.item: Offer the user the choice to merge the PR or leave it open for maintainer review without pre-evaluating permissions.
If user chooses to merge, attempt the merge directly. If the merge fails, report the error plainly, never claim false success, do not retry automatically, and proceed to workspace restoration.

Execute Phase 6 post-merge cleanup: return local workspace to main via git checkout main && git pull and delete feature branch upon successful merge (or keep remote branch intact if merge failed or was skipped).
Task completion is strictly invalid until Phase 6 is fully executed. Calling `attempt_completion` prematurely is strictly forbidden.

category.name: manual_closure_and_destructive_actions
category.item: For manual closures (not planned, duplicate): draft closure reason, comment, and label change; halt at explicit approval gate with turn separation before calling update_issue.

For any terminal or destructive action (branch deletion, issue closure, comment deletion): present specific candidate target and obtain explicit human confirmation in a subsequent turn, even when prompted with broad cleanup requests.
